page: Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-32 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine instance designed for workloads requiring an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio. The instance is provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 496.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 15.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include dedicated hardware accelerators, carrying a GPU count of zero.

Storage architecture requires external attachment, as the instance includes no local storage disks. Network access configurations also allocate zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default, necessitating external IP configuration or private routing for internet-bound traffic. System architectural extensions across vector computation, matrix processing, cryptography, and hardware-assisted virtualization flags are not enabled in this profile.

From an infrastructure perspective, the high density of 496.0 GB of memory across 32 vCPUs targets applications constrained primarily by memory footprint rather than parallel compute execution. This configuration yields qualitative resource efficiency by avoiding excessive CPU over-allocation when hosting massive datasets entirely within system RAM. The instance is positioned for large in-memory databases, heavy caching infrastructure, enterprise ERP frameworks, and real-time analytical engines.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-32 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 496.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory density of 15.5 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no integrated GPUs and does not come bundled with local disk storage, meaning persistent storage must be provisioned via attached network volumes. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default. Because of its large memory allocation relative to compute capacity, the instance offers cost-efficient utilization for memory-bound systems without requiring the over-provisioning of excess processor cores. Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-32 is structured for workloads such as large in-memory databases, distributed caches, enterprise transactional databases, and big data memory-resident analytics.
